newsitem.title: USA: U.S. may enhance troop security in Gulf.
newsitem.headline: U.S. may enhance troop security in Gulf.

text.p: The United States may take additional protective measures for U.S. troops in the Gulf based on a new report questioning security at some military and diplomatic posts in the area, Defence Secretary William Cohen said on Thursday.

"Anytime that anyone makes an assessment that we are in any way deficient, we take it very seriously," Cohen said in response to questions from reporters about the report on security from terrorism by a National Security Council analyst. "We will look at the Simon report very carefully and take whatever additional measures need to be taken."
The recent report by NSC official Steve Simon to the White House follows two terrorist car bombings in Saudi Arabia, one last June and the other in 1995, that killed a total of 24 U.S. troops.

The Washington Post reported on Thursday that Simon wrote in a memo that there were gaps in security at several facilities, including an air base in Kuwait where U.S. crews are stationed, an apartment building in Bahrain that houses U.S. naval personnel, a port in the United Arab Emirates where U.S. aircraft carriers dock and an American Embassy in the region.

"I'm familiar with the report that was filed with the NSC and others. We take it very seriously," said Cohen at a Pentagon photo opportunity with visiting Malaysian Defence Minister Syed Hamid Aibar. He noted that Deputy U.S. Defence Secretary John White was currently in the Gulf region on a long-planned visit and was studying security.

"But I should point out that we can never provide 100 percent full protection for our forces who are dispersed throughout the world," Cohen cautioned. "We will take whatever measures are necessary to provide the best possible guarantee against terrorist attacks against our forces, but there can be no 100 percent, fool-proof guarantee. And we understand that."
